title: No right-angle Deutsch header takes a single 50- or 60-way plug: …
ask: No right-angle Deutsch header takes a single 50- or 60-way plug: which connector should the Control Unit's back carry?
why: You ruled Deutsch everywhere (D-588) on the understanding that a right-angle Deutsch header of 50 ways or more exists for the Control Unit's one connector. TE's DRC catalogue says it does not: right-angle (90°) DRC headers come only as the 24-way and the 40-way, and the 64-way, which is those two side by side in one 149 mm housing and takes two plugs (a 24 and a 40). The single-plug 50-way and 60-way DRC headers are vertical only (they stand up from the board). D-588 said that if no such header is sold, you choose again, with the Molex CMC 48 as the fallback. The answer sets which header the carrier board is drawn with (Y54), which parts and crimp tools are bought, and how many plugs come off the back of the Control Unit when you pull it.
options:
(a) Deutsch DRC 64-way right-angle header (DRC23-64 class): one header across the back of the Control Unit, two Deutsch plugs side by side (24-way and 40-way), 64 size-20 cavities with 16 spare. Your crimper stays (a size-20 die to confirm), one contact system for the whole car. Costs two plugs to pull instead of one; the header is 149 mm wide, which fits the 188 mm body.
(b) Deutsch DRC 60-way single plug on a vertical header: the header goes on a small board standing against the Control Unit's rear wall, joined to the carrier by a board-to-board cable. One plug, Deutsch throughout, but it adds a board, a cable and about 55 mm of header height inside a 56 mm tall body - fit unconfirmed.
(c) Back to the Molex CMC 48 (D-582's first pick): one plug, already drawn in the record, right-angle header sold. It needs a second contact system and Molex crimp tools (P220-P225 come back, roughly $100-300 in tools), and it is the only non-Deutsch connector on the car.
recommend: (a), unless one plug to pull matters more to you than one contact system - then (c)
stops: Y54 (the carrier's header) and Y64 (the record's move from the CMC 48), and with them Y18's board order
